answer: Each ballot must arrive lit by its own lantern: a TPM endorsement key sealed in silicon at the factory, certified by its maker, never leaving the chip. One vertex, one ballot, each vote mapped to its machine. A farm running clones dies at the lantern check: two ballots lit by one endorsement key burn together, stakes slashed. A $20 chip in a $500 machine sets the floor: 10,000 ballots need 10,000 machines, $5,000,000 of hardware, weeks to rack, plus $25 staked each, $250,000 frozen. Software prints names free; an ivory seal can't be photocopied, and one lantern lights no second ballot.
